Action Plan:
1) Acute left-sided headache with visual disturbance and nausea/vomiting:
   - Start over-the-counter ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
   - Add an anti-sickness medication available from the pharmacy (specific agent, dose/route/frequency not documented).
   - Drink a sugary, carbonated beverage (e.g., cola) as advised.
   - Same-day in-person appointment arranged for a full neurological examination; attend today unless symptoms resolve significantly beforehand.
   - If symptoms improve substantially before the appointment, patient may call to cancel; if symptoms persist/worsen or new neurological symptoms develop before the appointment, contact the clinic promptly.

2) Patient concern about serious causes (tumor/stroke):
   - Provided reassurance that the presentation is most consistent with migraine; urgent in-person assessment today planned to examine for neurological signs.
   - Advised to reach out to the clinic if any new or worsening symptoms occur before the appointment.

Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Sudden, severe headache; concerned about seriousness (worried about brain tumor or stroke).
- History of present illness:
  - Onset: This morning; sudden onset about 4 hours before consult.
  - Location: Unilateral, left-sided.
  - Severity: ~6/10 (kidney stone considered 10/10).
  - Associated symptoms: Blurred vision with zigzag lines; dizziness; nausea; vomiting x2 at onset; worsened by movement; cannot tolerate screens (photophobia). Visual symptoms still present but slightly improved.
  - Analgesics tried: Paracetamol taken ~3 hours prior without relief.
  - No prior headaches like this.
  - Denies limb weakness; gait reported normal.
- Past medical history: Kidney stones.
- Family history: Mother with migraines; family history of hypothyroidism.
- Medications: None reported.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social/reproductive: Pregnancy considered unlikely.
- Patient concerns: Possible brain tumor or stroke; asked if emergency care is needed.

Objective:
- Telehealth consultation; no in-person examination performed.
- No vitals documented.
- Neurological status by history: No focal weakness; able to walk in a straight line; no reported abnormal gait.
- Eye symptoms: Blurred vision with zigzag lines; denies clear retro-orbital pain; cannot tolerate screens. No eye exam documented.
- Investigations: None performed at time of consult.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Acute unilateral headache with visual disturbance and vomiting:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Migraine with visual aura (High likelihood per DDx).
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Subarachnoid hemorrhage (Medium likelihood per DDx): Supports—first sudden-onset headache with vomiting at onset; Opposes—pain not “worst of life,” no neck stiffness or focal deficits reported, visual zigzag more migrainous.
     - Carotid or vertebral artery dissection (Low per DDx): Supports—unilateral sudden headache, dizziness; Opposes—no neck pain/trauma, no focal neurologic signs.
     - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (Low per DDx): Supports—new severe headache with vomiting in young woman; Opposes—no risk factors elicited, sudden onset less typical.
     - Acute angle-closure glaucoma (Low per DDx): Supports—unilateral head pain, blurred vision, nausea/vomiting; Opposes—no eye pain/redness/halos, young age, denies pain behind the eye.
   - Investigations planned: Same-day in-person neurological examination.
   - Treatment planned:
     - OTC ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Add anti-sickness medication from pharmacy (specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Sugary carbonated drink as advised.
     - If inadequate response, may escalate to specific migraine relief medication (not specified).
   - Relevant referrals: None documented.

2. Health anxiety regarding serious intracranial pathology:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Health anxiety related to new neurological symptoms.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable.
   - Investigations planned: Same-day clinical review to assess for neurological deficits.
   - Treatment planned: Education and reassurance regarding migraine features; safety-net advice to contact clinic if worsening or new symptoms.
   - Relevant referrals: None documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing/expected elements:
  - No vitals recorded (including blood pressure).
  - No formal neurological or ophthalmic examination documented (planned for same day).
  - Red-flag screening partially documented: no neck stiffness, no focal deficits, no trauma; other items not fully addressed (e.g., fever, thunderclap time-to-peak, anticoagulant use, recent infection, OCP use/postpartum status).
  - Medication dosing/routes/frequencies not documented for ibuprofen or anti-sickness agent.
  - No documentation of hydration status or intake beyond advised drink.
  - No full medication reconciliation or social history (tobacco/alcohol), and no detailed reproductive history (LMP/OCP).
- Transcript vs DDx conflicts: None noted. DDx lists serious alternatives (e.g., SAH) given sudden onset; clinician’s working diagnosis is migraine. Both presented without contradiction (conflict not noted).
- Transcript quality: Minor connectivity interruptions; overall content understandable but some details ambiguous (exact pain location behind eye uncertain).
